title: Antarctic Ice Marathon — Frequently asked questions
claims: The 2026 Antarctic Ice Marathon / Half Marathon is scheduled for 13 December 2026 and is the 21st edition.
Antarctic flights are not guaranteed to operate on schedule; days of delay can be normal and runners should allow at least two weeks after the expected return.
The departure point is Punta Arenas, Chile; runners arrange their own flights to Punta Arenas, typically via Santiago, and a Boeing 757 flies them about four hours to Union Glacier, landing at 80°S.
The marathon is normally run on a 10.55 km loop repeated four times, with an aid station every 5 km and a heated structure at the half-way point.
The marathon cut-off is 10 hours; the temperature at Union Glacier typically ranges from -10 °C to -20 °C at race time.
The course is groomed before the race and should be reasonably solid ice, but can include soft and loose snow; trail running shoes are recommended.
The race entry fee is USD 22,500; official hotels in Punta Arenas are Diego de Almagro and Almasur, and runners should budget for several days of possible delay.
Union Glacier camp has a basic medical clinic staffed by a doctor and medic specialising in emergency and remote medicine, with 24-hour support.
